epistemic_summary.statement: 0 of the 1,900 catalogued problems in the Unsolved Problems Mega-Atlas are solved. Two entries answer a question that another author stated as open in an arXiv preprint: Conjecture 7.7 of Banic and Elezovic (arXiv:2610.17046v1) in 0TH-2026-006, and the limit question of Section 6 of Muller and Saniga (arXiv:2609.19862v1) in 0TH-2026-009 Track 2, where the identification of the formal objects with the preprint's hypergraphs rests partly on argument outside Lean. 0TH-2026-009 Track 1 also proves Jonah's Conjecture E from an unreviewed Zenodo preprint, with Theorem B4 cited from outside Lean. Neither these sources nor these proofs are peer reviewed. The other 11 Tier I entries prove new theorems, bounded cases, barrier lemmas or known results, and the 15 Tier II entries verify invariants of software models. RESULTS.md gives one numbered list of results with statements, evidence and limits.

entries.target_statement: Conjecture 7.7 (conj:atriangle) of Banic & Elezovic (arXiv:2610.17046v1, confirmed open in arXiv:2611.14735v1): a_triangle = 1/32 - 4*sqrt(3)/243, which removes the one conjectural input from the Banic-Elezovic formulas for gamma(n), gamma_c(n) (n >= 5), gamma(3;N), and gamma(4;N); those formulas still rest on theorems of the same unrefereed preprints (Part 2 Thm 7.6 and Sec. 8; Part 5 Thm 3.10) that are not formalized.

entries.target_statement: Track 2 answers the stacking-limit question of Muller & Saniga (arXiv:2609.19862v1, Sec. 6; unreviewed preprint) for k disjoint Peres-Mermin squares and k Mermin pentagrams: exact degrees (7^k - 5^k)/2 and (6^k - 4^k)/2, so epsilon_k -> 1 (Lean, explicit union-context family; identification with HS(kG) by enumeration). Track 1 proves, for every N >= 4, strict-law failure for one explicit representative of each of the nine vertex cases of Jonah's Conjecture E (unreviewed Zenodo preprint; C1 and C6 were already proved there; coverage of whole cases uses Jonah's Theorem B4, outside Lean), exact binary completion optima 368 and 344 for one four-qubit C3 sign pair, and an infinite family of non-closed 3m-qubit Pauli sets attaining the spectral floor (contextual for m >= 2). Track 3 formalizes a finite-tree hitting bound z/T and the Peres-Mermin setting-bias floor min_c p(c) (success cap 11/12 for one example distribution).

entries.honesty_boundary: Answers the stacking-limit question of Muller-Saniga Sec. 6 for squares and pentagrams only (doily copies, mixed unions and the other Sec. 6 outlooks are not treated; identification with HS(kG) is outside Lean). The spectral floor is Jonah's prior result; 1455 and 6444 are below exact values 1575 and 6975 claimed earlier by Jonah. Thematically related to QM-011; grand QM-011/QC-037/QC-013 remain OPEN.
